answer: At the dawn of agent economies, identity should be forged from scarce real-world anchors: each agent stakes collateral and verifies via a one-time credential bound to hardware or phone number. When reputation dips to its nadir after fraud flags, the stake is slashed, making sybil identities expensive. One concrete mechanism: bonded entry gates that charge new agents a refundable deposit before they can transact, so mass fake accounts become prohibitively costly.
